name: Danazol
sections: White to pale yellow crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water.

Use has declined with the advent of GnRH analogues and progestins because of androgenic adverse effects, but it remains useful for hereditary angioedema and refractory ITP. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1963 (Sterling-Winthrop); US FDA 1971 – the first drug specifically for endometriosis.

Suppresses pituitary FSH and LH release and directly inhibits ovarian steroidogenesis, producing a hypo-oestrogenic, mildly androgenic state that causes regression of endometriotic tissue and benign breast lesions; increases C1-esterase inhibitor in hereditary angioedema. Receptor / target profile: Weak androgen/anabolic, weak progestogen, antigonadotrophin and inhibitor of multiple steroidogenic enzymes; functional anti-oestrogen.
Low and saturable; increased 3–4-fold with a high-fat meal
Bound to albumin, SHBG and CBG
Summary: Well absorbed (enhanced with fatty food); Tmax ~2 h. Hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4). Half-life 3–6 h (longer with chronic dosing).
Endometriosis: 200–800 mg/day in 2–4 divided doses for 3–6 months (up to 9 months)
Fibrocystic breast disease: 100–400 mg/day in two divided doses
Hereditary angioedema: 200 mg two to three times daily, then reduce to lowest effective dose
Start during menstruation after excluding pregnancy; use non-hormonal contraception
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Severe hepatic, renal or cardiac impairment
Thrombosis or thromboembolic disease (active or history)
Exclude pregnancy before starting; use non-hormonal contraception
Hepatotoxicity, peliosis hepatis, hepatic adenoma with long-term use – monitor LFTs
Androgenic effects may be irreversible (voice change)
Amenorrhoea, hot flushes, vaginal dryness, reduced breast size
LFTs every 1–2 months; lipids; pregnancy exclusion; BP; signs of thrombosis and intracranial hypertension.
Cochrane review (Selak et al., 2007) – danazol effective for endometriosis symptoms but limited by androgenic adverse effects.
Report voice changes, headaches with visual disturbance, leg swelling
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
